passage: On Monday, Uday dropped the steel tumbler and milk splashed across the kitchen floor. Papa's voice from the next room was already booming, "What was that?" Uday whispered, "Not me," and hid behind the door, his heart pounding. On Wednesday he cracked a plate and slid the pieces under the cupboard. On Saturday, a new plate slipped and broke. Papa Harsha came in quietly and said, "I would rather know than have a broken plate hidden. I won't shout at you." Uday's hands trembled. He took a slow breath and said, "It was me." Papa nodded and knelt down to help him sweep.

qa.q: Where did Uday hide the pieces of the cracked plate?
qa.a: Uday slid the pieces under the cupboard.

qa.q: What was Uday feeling on Monday when he said "Not me"?
qa.a: Uday was afraid of Papa's booming voice. The fear was bigger than his wish to be honest, so he hid behind the door with a pounding heart.

qa.q: What changed on Saturday that let Uday tell the truth?
qa.a: Papa Harsha stayed quiet and promised not to shout, so telling felt safe. Safe truth-telling at home makes children more honest.

qa.q: How might Papa Harsha have seen Uday's hiding on Wednesday?
qa.a: Papa may have wondered why Uday hid things instead of telling him. The hiding may be a sign that Uday was scared, not simply naughty.

grounding: A child lies because he fears being scolded, the fear stronger than the wish to be honest, until a parent makes truth safe.
